ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: What is the pollen-bearing part of the stamen?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached flower diagram shows a flower cross-section. On each side there is a stamen-like structure with a thin stalk and an oval tip. A right-side bracket groups the stamen parts, and the oval tip is the part associated with pollen. Reasoning: The question asks for the pollen-bearing part of the stamen. In flower anatomy, a stamen consists of a filament and an anther. The anther is the oval tip of the stamen and is where pollen is produced or borne. Therefore, the pollen-bearing part of the stamen is the anther.
